neighbours.label: A positive evaluation word (good, better, guarantee, effective) at a point where the good is being limited or denied ('hardly a guarantee', 'never … for the better', 'which is good, but')
fire: A high salary is hardly a guarantee of a happy life.
Yelling at people never changes them for the better.
The rain has stopped, which is good, but the fields are still flooded.
We had hoped the repair would buy us a few good months, but sadly the engine died within a week.
A famous name is no guarantee of quality in this business.
The fever is down, which is good, but his cough is still bad.
Constant criticism rarely changes a team for the better.
They promised the upgrade would bring several good years, but sadly the system crashed in a month.
quiet: A high salary is paid to the engineers at this firm.
Yelling at people was common in the old market square.
The rain has stopped and the fields are drying in the wind.
We took the car to the shop and the engine was replaced within a week.
A famous name is printed on the label of each bottle.
The fever is measured twice a day with a small device.
Constant traffic passes the stadium on the way to the port.
They installed the upgrade in March and restarted the system at noon.

notes: Card flags the pole broad (1.2% of tokens reach 0.1 of max). Top examples sit on a good outcome that is about to be undercut; the - pole promotes ' worse', ' worst', ' burden'. Probes: such sentences 0.33-0.52 (peak ' good', ' guarantee', ' better'), plain positive 0.08-0.24, neutral description 0.02.
